key_insight: Pauli propagation enables classical pre-training of large, shallow parametrized quantum circuits while leaving target states or samples classically intractable.
engineering_relevance: Classical pre-training reduces reliance on costly quantum gradient estimation and supplies parameters ready for deployment on quantum hardware.
method: Propagate observables backward through the circuit to derive a parametric loss expression.
Use weight- and degree-based truncation plus pruning to control propagation cost.
Optimize parameters classically, then deploy the trained circuits on quantum hardware.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 64-qubit demonstrations for a two-dimensional Ising VQE and binary-image generation, with pre-trained parameters deployed on IBM's ibm_berlin processor.
watch_item: Truncation and pruning make propagation tractable but require checking approximation error and its effect on hardware performance.
paper_title: Classical Pre-Training of Large Shallow Parametrized Quantum Circuits through Pauli Propagation and deployment on Quantum Hardware
